messages.subject: accessing other modification indices
parts:
Hello,

I have been working on a program in R for a group search algorithm that utilizes lavaan; lavaan has been quite helpful thus far. As part of our program, the model selection procedure begins by running the null model on each participant's data. Modification indices are then used to iteratively select paths that improve fit for the majority of individuals. There are many other steps, but that is the only portion relevant to my question. 

For the models where we begin estimation with the autoregressive paths in place, lavaan provides all modification indices of interest for the beta matrix. However, now that I am working on code for the option of beginning estimation without the autoregressive paths open, I find that lavaan does not provide the MIs of interest to us. Of course, this makes sense, as lavaan doesn't provide MIs for the beta matrix when nothing is being estimated in the beta matrix.

My question: is there a way to coerce lavaan into providing the MIs for the beta matrix when starting with a null model? It's possible in LISREL, but I have not yet been able to figure it out in lavaan. 

Any ideas would be greatly appreciated. Thanks much. 

Stephanie

messages.author: 3fe90052fbf2f899
messages.subject: Re: accessing other modification indices
parts:
I'm guessing you have time-series data, running a p-technique type of analysis, since you are investigating fit for different individuals...  Regardless, if the problem is that there is no beta matrix in the null model, you can add one in a way that should not affect the fit or degrees of freedom for the null model.

Generate a vector of random numbers (normal, uniform, whatever), and regress that vector on all the variables in your model.  Save the residuals in another vector, which is then a vector of random numbers that are completely orthogonal to all variables in the model (correlations = 0).  You could also do this in a single step:

myData$ranOrth <- resid(lm(rnorm(nrow(myData)) ~ myData$var1 + myData$var2 + ... + myData$varN))

Since ranOrth is uncorrelated with any variable, you can run the null model as before, but additionally fix the correlations of all other variables with ranOrth to zero, except for one.  For one of the original model variables, specify instead that the regression path to ranOrth is zero.  I haven't tried it yet, but that should introduce the beta matrix into the model, allowing you to view MIs, but without changing the degrees of freedom or the (lack of) fit, since the observed associations are actually null to begin with.  But check those values, because I may not be thinking of everything.  Oh, and if you are analyzing the covariance matrix and mean vector instead of raw data, it is easy to simply use cbind() and rbind() to add a row/column of zeros corresponding to another orthogonal variable, specifying a nonzero variance for it.

Terry

messages.author: 89c9fc822e34b78c
messages.subject: Re: accessing other modification indices
parts:
On 09/12/2013 02:16 PM, Stephanie Lane wrote:

> My question: is there a way to coerce lavaan into providing the MIs for
> the beta matrix when starting with a null model?

Yes. You need to add an 'empty' regression (fixed to zero). But take
care that you still have same free parameters as in the original model.

Eg, for the holzinger & swineford example, you could do:

HS.model <- ' visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9

visual ~~ textual + speed
textual ~~ speed

visual ~ 0*speed
'

fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)

This will give you an identical fit, but with an (empty) beta matrix.

Yves.
